newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Oil prices to rise after seasonal lows-Lukman.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices to rise after seasonal lows-Lukman.

text.p: OPEC's Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman said on Tuesday oil prices would rise to up to $21 a barrel after the end of summer in the northern hemisphere.

"Once the current seasonal conditions are passed, oil prices will be between $19 and $21 a barrel but for sure they will not reach the 1996 level of between $24 and $25," he told the Kuwait News Agency (KUNA) in an interview.
Lukman is on a visit of the United Arab Emirates with OPEC President Abdullah Salem al-Badri, also Libya's oil minister.
He said the "extraordinary circumstances" which led to the high price levels in 1996 were not on the horizon, urging OPEC members to "look carefully" at the elements which affect the world market.
But he noted the $2 rise in the past few days to over a $19 a barrel.
When asked if OPEC would review quotas at the June ministerial meeting, Lukman said: "What is being debated now is respecting quotas not cutting them."
According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), production by the 11-nation OPEC hit 27.13 million barrels per day (bpd) compared with a set ceiling of 25.05 million bpd.

"We are trying to convince everyone with the importance of abiding by quotas and are also trying to convince producers and consumers with the importance of the market's stability," Lukman told the Kuwaiti agency.
He said world demand was constantly rising, Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil producer and exporter with an eight million bpd output, had an "idle" production capacity of two million bpd.

Kuwait and the UAE have a "stopped" production capacity of one million bpd while Iraq, once United Nations sanctions are lifted, could enter the market with between two million and 2.5 million bpd, added Lukman.
